inline_comments.comment:
There is no way to opt out of the reload button. `onReloadStory` is unconditionally set to `handleReloadStory` for every inline story, which causes `withToolbar || !!onReloadStory` in `Preview.tsx` to always be `true`. This silently overrides an explicit `withToolbar: false` set via `parameters.docs.canvas.withToolbar` or the `withToolbar` prop on `<Canvas>`. A user who deliberately suppressed the toolbar will see it reappear after this change.

Consider gating the reload handler on the resolved `withToolbar` value, e.g.:
```tsx
onReloadStory={inline && withToolbar ? handleReloadStory : undefined}
```
Or introduce a separate opt-out escape hatch (e.g., `withReloadButton` prop or a `parameters.docs.canvas.withReloadButton` parameter) and document how to disable it.

The `key="reload"` prop on this `Button` is unnecessary. React only uses `key` for reconciliation of elements in an array (e.g., returned from `.map()`). This element is inside a fragment, not an array, so the prop is silently ignored by React and misleads future readers into thinking it serves a purpose. Remove it. The pre-existing `<Wrapper key="left">` in the parent is unrelated — that `key` is on the wrapper itself, not on its non-array children.

The reload button provides no visual feedback after it is clicked. The manager's equivalent remount tool (`code/core/src/manager/components/preview/tools/remount.tsx`) listens for the `FORCE_REMOUNT` event on the channel and applies a CSS rotation animation to `SyncIcon` for the duration of the remount, giving the user clear confirmation the action registered. The docs button just fires `onClick` with no state change, so a user who clicks it cannot tell whether the click was received or the remount is in progress. Consider adding the same animation pattern (or a simpler `isRemounting` boolean state toggled on click and cleared on the next render) to match the established UX.

general_comments.comment:
The PR adds new user-visible behaviour — a reload button, `FORCE_REMOUNT` emission, and conditional toolbar visibility — but the entire testing checklist is unchecked and no tests of any kind are included.

At minimum, the PR should add:
1. **Unit test** — assert that clicking (or calling) the reload handler emits `FORCE_REMOUNT` with the correct `storyId` on the docs channel. A mock of `docsContext.channel.emit` makes this straightforward.
2. **Story update** — add a variant to `Preview.stories.tsx` (or a new `Canvas.stories.tsx` entry) that passes `onReloadStory` and includes a `play` function verifying the reload `Button` is present in the DOM and fires the callback when clicked.
3. **Negative case** — a test or story asserting the reload button is absent when `inline` is `false` (the iframe path), so the conditional at `Canvas.tsx:99` is explicitly covered.
